note: Lumen Gentium reiterates the irreformability of papal definitions. This identifies a shared doctrinal assertion, not a claim that every sentence in either passage is a definition.

evidence.quote: his definitions, of themselves, and not from the consent of the Church, are justly styled irreformable
such definitions of the Roman Pontiff from himself, but not from the consensus of the Church, are unalterable

note: The responsum explicitly addresses the status of the teaching in Ordinatio Sacerdotalis, rather than announcing a new papal ex cathedra definition.

evidence.quote: which is presented in the Apostolic Letter Ordinatio Sacerdotalis to be held definitively
this judgment is to be definitively held by all the Church's faithful

note: The responsum cites Lumen Gentium 25, paragraph 2, when explaining the ordinary and universal magisterium.

evidence.quote: cf. Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church Lumen Gentium 25, 2
they are in agreement on one position as definitively to be held

note: Ministeria Quaedam expressly quotes LG 10 on the relation between the common and ministerial priesthood. Translation wording differs between these local selections.

evidence.quote: the common priesthood of the faithful and the ministerial or hierarchical priesthood, though they differ in essence and not only in degree
the common priesthood of the faithful and the ministerial or hierarchical priesthood are nonetheless interrelated

note: Traditionis Custodes changes the framework for use of the 1962 Missal and abrogates incompatible prior norms. This relationship concerns discipline; it does not identify a reversal of dogma or claim every earlier norm was abrogated.

evidence.quote: Previous norms, instructions, permissions, and customs that do not conform to the provisions of the present Motu Proprio are abrogated.
For such a celebration with either Missal, the priest needs no permission from the Apostolic See or from his own Ordinary.

note: The accompanying CDF letter explains the reasoning behind the 2018 Catechism revision. This relationship does not resolve the separate disputed question of continuity with earlier teaching.

evidence.quote: the increasing understanding that the dignity of a person is not lost even after committing the most serious crimes
there is an increasing awareness that the dignity of the person is not lost even after the commission of very serious crimes
